title: The 7 Lies of Learning
coreMove: Audit a learning myth by the behavior it produces, then replace it with a testable rule.
sourcePressure: The chapter clears common myths that keep learners passive, intimidated, dependent, or too quick to surrender.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Inventing an exact seven-item list unsupported by the frozen source.
sourceAnchorNote: Frozen sidecar contains no chapter-local named figure, named study, named place, or dated anecdote. Use fictional protagonists and keep source alignment at the concept and title-pressure level.

hook: Do not open The 7 Lies of Learning with a generic unlocked potential claim.
Do not start with a definition of the 7 lies of learning.
counterintuition: Do not use a not X but Y correction shell.
Do not claim the opposite of common sense in generic coaching language.
tryThisNow: Do not use set a timer and reflect.
Do not ask the reader to journal broadly without a visible action.
examples: No repeated desk, kitchen, classroom, commute, or generic meeting shells.
No six examples built around timestamp plus named protagonist plus decision.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: patron who thinks older adults cannot learn new apps
exampleSpecs.stakes: she needs the portal to renew housing forms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie asks what action the belief prevents, then has the patron complete one renewal step while naming the myth as a guess.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a library mouse pad worn smooth at the edge

exampleSpecs.audience: mechanic who thinks real learners never ask basic questions
exampleSpecs.stakes: a customer's race setup depends on correct sag measurement
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Henrik writes the embarrassing question on the work order and gets the measurement method right before touching the shock.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a shock pump clipped to a repair stand

exampleSpecs.audience: volunteer believes memory should work after one reading
exampleSpecs.stakes: families wait while she rereads the same checklist
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chiara notices the myth by the delay it creates, then builds a three-card retrieval stack for intake steps.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: passport photocopies under a binder clip

exampleSpecs.audience: assistant believes mistakes mean he lacks the knack
exampleSpecs.stakes: a contaminated batch can waste a week of production
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas predicts which step failed, checks the log, and replaces the knack story with a sanitation checklist test.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: foam residue clinging to a sample tube

exampleSpecs.audience: actor believes accents require natural mimicry
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia breaks the accent into one mouth position and records ten lines to test a practice rule against the myth.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pencil tucked across a marked script

exampleSpecs.audience: organizer thinks learning styles mean she cannot learn from diagrams
exampleSpecs.stakes: spring seedlings are failing under the lights
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hadiya tries the diagram plus one hands-on tray and records which instruction actually changed the seed depth.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: peat cells lined under purple grow lights

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm, using a question to the reader, a research aside only if source-supported, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: Identify when audit a learning myth by the behavior it produces, then replace it with a testable rule. is needed in a new scenario.
Choose the visible action that matches The 7 Lies of Learning rather than a nearby generic lesson.
Explain why the weak alternative fails without using recall-only phrasing.

tryThisNowSpec: Name one learning myth by the behavior it causes, then choose one small test that would challenge it today.
